_palette_correction: E12 Ruling 12e. The fixture named five of eleven elements in the pale-bone family and the literal word 'bone' rode this string FIVE times; under the ruled ultra-realistic register it rendered literally, and on BOTH measured seeds the tail's banded underside and the blade rows read as exposed skeleton while family pressure invented ivory ridges on SMOOTH leg geometry and on D1-declared wing fingers. 'bone' now appears twice and 'ivory' three times, all three at the head (D4 horns, D5 crown and cheek spikes, D10 fangs). MEASURED CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FILE, stated because it is checkable: view 5's stem drops the mouth family and the horn family, so after the correction it contains NO pale-bone-family word at all - the cleanest available test of whether the word was the mechanism. View 1 carries all three.
_companion_stem: headclay_0 is the handoff-5 head-crop companion at yaw 0, frame 1360x1360, ortho_scale 0.223104. Element visibility was VERIFIED against its own clay render (headclay_y+000.png) before the v4 stem was written; that verification is geometric and the correction does not disturb it. KEEPS D3 storm-grey wing membranes - BOTH wings enter the crop at the left and right edges, large areas, exactly the case Gate 0 flagged as membrane passing behind the skull on this mesh. DROPS D6 (dorsal and TAIL spines - the tail is far out of frame) and D7 (claws - the feet are out of frame and no wing-claw spur is legible at the edges). The subject noun 'a winged dragon,' STAYS: identity rides the prompt, and composition is held by the control. NOT SUBMITTED at handoff 6 - the companion is not re-run (Ruling 12f); this stem is built so the file stays complete and the cloud guard's provenance check keeps working without a skip flag.
_companion_rationale_VOID: EXECUTOR FLAG for the advisor, reported and NOT repaired from this seat. v4's justification for dropping D6 from headclay_0 had a second clause - 'the ivory family is already carried by D4/D5/D10, so the shoulder-end spines at the bottom edge keep their colour by family'. That clause is VOID under Ruling 12e: D6 is now charcoal, a family no other term in the companion stem carries, so the shoulder-end spines entering the companion's bottom edge have NO declared colour. The out-of-frame clause (the tail) still stands on its own and is why the drop is built as the dispatch instructs. Whether the companion's stem should keep D6 when it is next generated is a fixture question for the advisor.
